reason: Launch claims (user, roles, context) arrive in an RS256-signed JWT whose KID is checked against the platform's well-known key (C1, C2), and the tool can confirm the membership claim by querying NRPS on the platform, which is the system of record for course membership, and can read back line items it wrote via AGS (C3). Other content: Deep Linking items are signed but unverifiable beyond C2.

Roster records are schema-checked by the validator (C1) and in REST mode come from an OAuth-authenticated SIS endpoint (C2); the receiver can query the SIS, which the spec names as the source of roster data, to confirm an enrollment (C3). CSV drops carry no signature and reach only C1 unless reconciled against the SIS; gradebook data flows the other way and is not independently checkable.

Credentials are JSON-schema checked and signed as Verifiable Credentials with a revocation status check (C1, C2), but the spec states verification 'does not imply evaluation of the truth of claims' and validation is 'outside the scope'; the issuer is the claimant itself, so no separate authority for the achievement is reachable. Endorsements add signed third-party opinion, still C2.

A content package checked by the member validator for 'error-free import' (C1); the standard defines no signature or issuer authentication for the package, and there is no authority for whether the textbook content is correct. Embedded LTI links inherit LTI checks only at launch.

Item and test packages are validated 'for structural consistency against the QTI 3 standard' (C1); packages carry no issuer signature and no authority exists to confirm an item's scoring key or quality. Results reporting is also unsigned.

Frameworks are JSON-schema checked (C1) and fetched over TLS from a CASE server; the receiver can retrieve the canonical CFItem by URI from the issuing agency's server, the authority for the 'official statement of the competency' (C3), though no message signature exists. Alignments of resources to items are a separate claim with no check beyond C1.

Same VC model as Open Badges: schema, signature and revocation checks (C1, C2), and the spec repeats that verification 'does not imply evaluation of the truth of claims'; CLR 1.0 names the issuer 'the authoritative source' for its own assertion, so consulting it only re-confirms provenance. Transcript-type entries could be checked against a registrar outside the standard.

Person, section and enrollment records come over an OpenAPI REST interface with required OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens (C1, C2), and the receiver can query the SIS, which the spec names as 'the system of record' and most common provider, to confirm a record (C3).

Events must carry required properties and valid JSON-LD envelopes (C1) and are posted to an endpoint that authenticates the sensor by token (C2, weak: no per-event signature); whether the learner actually did the reported action is witnessed only by the sensor, and the spec offers no authority to consult.

People, groups and memberships are exchanged via SOAP web services profiled for SIS to LMS (C1, C2 via authenticated service calls), and the LMS can read memberships directly from the SIS, the source system for enrollment (C3). Outcomes flowing back to the SIS are not independently checkable.
